{

  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Cached line data",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "Words stored in the cache data memory and used to satisfy cache hits or refill cache lines. The cache depends on this data to return host read results without a backing-bus transfer.",

        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"

      "Rubric Reason": "The data can contain integrator-sensitive information and is exposed through host_rsp_o.data at line 156. Cache writes and refill writes can alter it through lines 414-423, so unauthorized modification can return incorrect data.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could inject or alter a cache write or refill value and could observe the resulting cached word through a host read response.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "host_req_i.data",
        "bus_rsp_i.data"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "host_rsp_o.data"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        151,
        236
      ],

        414,
        417,
        420,

        428

      "Exit Lines": [
        156
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Cache access address",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The address selecting the cache line, word and backing-bus location for an access. Correct address selection is required to read or update the intended cached data and to issue the corresponding refill request.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The address is material to correct cache and backing-memory accesses because host_req_i.addr forms cache_o.addr and the stored tag/index at lines 149, 180 and 181. Altering the address can select or update the wrong line or backing word, threatening integrity.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter the access address so that the cache returns or overwrites a different line than the one requested.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "host_req_i.addr"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_req_o.addr"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        149,
        180,
        181

        149,

        225,

      ],

        159,
        227,
        238
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Cache hit decision",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The decision that an addressed cache entry is valid and has the requested tag. It determines whether the unit acknowledges or writes the cache directly or starts a backing-bus transaction; it has no direct unit-port entry or exit because it is generated internally and used as control.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Valid and tag state together with the access address produce hit_o at line 405, and the decision selects acknowledgement, cache writing and bus activity at line 189, so corrupting it can produce an incorrect access result.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could manipulate the cache metadata or hit path so a miss is treated as a hit, or a hit is repeatedly sent through the refill path and withholds normal completion.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        405
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Cache bypass routing decision",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The decision that routes an access around the cache, including accesses classified as uncacheable, atomic or debug accesses. It determines whether the cache or the backing bus handles the transfer and has no direct port carrying the decision itself.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "yes"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The bypass decision controls bus strobe, cache write and response behavior through ctrl.buf_dir at lines 173, 186 and 187, so changing it can route an access incorrectly and threaten integrity.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could force the unchecked debug, atomic or address classification to use the wrong path, causing incorrect results or making normal transfers depend on an unavailable backing bus.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        126,
        173
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C5",
      "Concept Name": "Cache line fill control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The internal command that starts and commits population of a cache line after a miss. It controls whether refill data and its corresponding cache metadata become usable, with no direct unit-port entry or exit.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The fill command is produced at line 226 and causes cache-line population through the memory instance, so altering it can commit data to the wrong cache state or prevent a miss from completing.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could suppress or force a line fill so stale or wrong data is marked usable, or so cache misses repeatedly fail to complete.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        226
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C6",
      "Concept Name": "Cache flush and fence control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The pending fence request and its resulting cache-clear operation. It is used to discard cached state and synchronize the backing bus before subsequent accesses.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "A host fence is stored in ctrl.buf_sync and drives cache clearing at lines 138, 126 and 219, so unauthorized alteration can remove or retain cache state incorrectly.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could assert or suppress the fence request to flush valid cache state unexpectedly or prevent a required synchronization and delay later transfers.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "host_req_i.fence"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "bus_req_o.fence"

        138

        219
      ],

        217
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C7",
      "Concept Name": "Cache invalidation control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The internal command that invalidates a cache entry after a refill error. It controls whether an affected cached entry remains eligible for use and has no direct unit-port entry or exit.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The invalidation command is generated at line 255 from the recorded refill error and changes cache validity through the memory instance, so unauthorized alteration can leave bad state usable or discard usable state.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could force or suppress invalidation after a failed refill, causing stale data to remain active or forcing repeated refills and transfer failures.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        255
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C8",
      "Concept Name": "Backing-bus error status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Information": "The error condition returned by the backing bus and recorded during cache-line download. It determines whether the refill is rejected and is reported to the host as an error.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The bus error is recorded in ctrl.buf_err at lines 242 and 126 and changes invalidation and host error behavior at lines 254-257, so modifying it can make the cache report the wrong result.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could inject or suppress a backing-bus error so a failed refill is accepted as valid or a successful transfer is rejected and withheld.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "bus_rsp_i.err"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "host_rsp_o.err"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        242
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        126,
        242
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        209,
        257
      ]
    }
  ],

    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Build-time cache configuration",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "NUM_BLOCKS, BLOCK_SIZE, UC_BEGIN and READ_ONLY are generics that only fix the build and cannot be changed or withheld at run time."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Forwarded bus transactions and relayed data",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The host and backing-bus request or response portions that are only forwarded, including direct-path data, are excluded as forwarded transactions or relayed data; only data stored in the cache is kept in C1."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Cache tag and valid copies",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The tag and valid memories only record which backing words are cached, so the cached-copies rule excludes them as pieces of their own."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Controller sequencing state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "ctrl.state and the refill offset sequencing state only order transfers and steps, so the sequencing-state rule excludes them."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Pending request and handshake bookkeeping",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "ctrl.buf_req and the acknowledge or strobe bookkeeping only re-time or complete the access already carried by the bus transaction."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Bus access command fields",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",

    },
    {

      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cache",
      "Merged Into": "C2",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.rubric reason: The data can contain integrator-sensitive information and is exposed through host_rsp_o.data at line 156. Cache writes and refill writes can alter it through lines 414-423, so unauthorized modification can return incorrect data.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could inject or alter a cache write or refill value and could observe the resulting cached word through a host read response.

conceptual assets.rubric reason: The address is material to correct cache and backing-memory accesses because host_req_i.addr forms cache_o.addr and the stored tag/index at lines 149, 180 and 181. Altering the address can select or update the wrong line or backing word, threatening integrity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the access address so that the cache returns or overwrites a different line than the one requested.

conceptual assets.information: The decision that an addressed cache entry is valid and has the requested tag. It determines whether the unit acknowledges or writes the cache directly or starts a backing-bus transaction; it has no direct unit-port entry or exit because it is generated internally and used as control.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Valid and tag state together with the access address produce hit_o at line 405, and the decision selects acknowledgement, cache writing and bus activity at line 189, so corrupting it can produce an incorrect access result.

conceptual assets.rubric reason: The bypass decision controls bus strobe, cache write and response behavior through ctrl.buf_dir at lines 173, 186 and 187, so changing it can route an access incorrectly and threaten integrity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the unchecked debug, atomic or address classification to use the wrong path, causing incorrect results or making normal transfers depend on an unavailable backing bus.

conceptual assets.information: The internal command that starts and commits population of a cache line after a miss. It controls whether refill data and its corresponding cache metadata become usable, with no direct unit-port entry or exit.

considered, not kept.concept: Forwarded bus transactions and relayed data
considered, not kept.reason: The host and backing-bus request or response portions that are only forwarded, including direct-path data, are excluded as forwarded transactions or relayed data; only data stored in the cache is kept in C1.
The tag and valid memories only record which backing words are cached, so the cached-copies rule excludes them as pieces of their own.
ctrl.state and the refill offset sequencing state only order transfers and steps, so the sequencing-state rule excludes them.
ctrl.buf_req and the acknowledge or strobe bookkeeping only re-time or complete the access already carried by the bus transaction.
The strobe, read/write direction, byte enables and similar access fields are part of the access they qualify rather than separate information under the access-command and forwarded-transaction rules.
